title: Machine learning development for quantum computing and neutrino physics
summary: This thesis investigates the application of machine-learning methods in the context of quantum computing and neutrino physics, with particular emphasis on the construction of effective representations for complex, high-dimensional data. The first part of the work is devoted to Quantum Extreme Learning Machines (QELMs), a hybrid quantum--classical framework in which classical data are encoded into quantum states and processed through fixed quantum dynamics, while learning is performed by a classical readout layer.
